result.title: Motion Beyond Pixels: Learning Future Visual Representations for Object-Centric Dynamics
result.summary: Many embodied world models predict future states in latent spaces optimized for RGB reconstruction, which do not explicitly prioritize object-level semantics and geometry relevant to motion generation. We present MotionRep, a visual representation world model that jointly generates future DINO representations and 3D object flow, coupling semantic and geometric information with object-centric dynamics. To make high-dimensional DINO features amenable to generative modeling, we introduce DINO-VAE, which combines temporal and channel compression with latent regularization to produce compact latents while preserving semantic and geometric information. Conditioned on an initial observation, object query points, and a language instruction, a unified diffusion transformer predicts future visual representations and 3D object flow through joint attention. MotionRep employs asymmetric modality-specific noise schedules to keep the visual stream ahead of 3D object flow during joint denoising, allowing progressively refined future visual representations to guide flow generation. Experiments on simulated and real-world manipulation benchmarks demonstrate that MotionRep outperforms pixel-based baselines in 3D object flow accuracy and generalization to unseen scenes, while requiring only three denoising steps for inference. These results support predictive visual representations as an effective future-state space for object-centric dynamics modeling.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MotionRep 世界模型：用 DINO-VAE 对高维 DINO 特征做时序与通道压缩，再以统一 diffusion transformer 在初始观测、物体查询点和语言指令条件下联合预测未来 DINO 表示与 3D object flow，并用非对称噪声调度让视觉流先于几何流。
AI.relevance_reason: 「以预测式视觉潜表示作为未来状态空间」与 LVR 关心的 latent 是否保留视觉细节和几何、以及表示如何被后续使用直接相关，可供核查其 DINO 潜空间压缩与信息保留情况；但该工作是具身操作动力学预测，而非 VLM 推理，迁移需较多核查。
